newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan, U.S. agree to strike air deal by end-Sept.
newsitem.headline: Japan, U.S. agree to strike air deal by end-Sept.

text.p: Japan and the United States have agreed to strike a new air deal covering both passenger and cargo traffic by the end of September, a Japanese Transport Ministry official said on Friday.
The agreement was made after three days of talks in Portland, Oregon.

Negotiations to lay the groundwork for the deal will be held in early August in Tokyo and will shift from an informal level to a formal level, the official said. At a formal level airline representatives are allowed to observe the discussions.
The two countries have been holding informal discussions on an irregular basis since early this year to resolve their decades-old aviation dispute and set the stage for a more liberal accord.
Japanese officials have said a new accord would most likely cover three to five years.
The official said an offer to set September as the target for reaching a deal was made by the United States, which is eager to resolve the dispute over air cargo.
U.S. cargo carrier Federal Express is seeking an expansion in its so-called beyond rights, the right to fly on to a third country, in particular to China.
But the official said the two sides were still at odds over whether "open skies" should be the principle behind air deregulation.
Washington wants any new accord to be a step along the way towards an ultimate goal of open skies, or the lifting of all government restrictions except safety and security rules.
Tokyo says that, while it is aiming for wide-scale deregulation, the U.S.-led policy only leads to monopolistic alliances dominated by U.S. air carriers.
